chapter: Dancing schools, Sapiro and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Musicians' clubs and hangouts on 131st and 133rd Streets
summary: He lists the Band Box, the Rhythm Club and Parson Jerry's, where Willie the Lion played, and recalls downtown society people strolling Harlem at night.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Were there certain places where musicians used to hang out?

One -- there used to be musicians' clubs, and one place was called the Band Box. The Band Box was on 131st Street, off of 7th Avenue. Then later on the Rhythm Club, the Rhythm Club. Then up on 133rd Street, where -- what was the name of that place? I can't remember the name of it. Then across the street -- 133rd Street was the place where there were a whole lot of places. There was one place, Parson Jerry's. Willy "the Lion" used to play there. And what's the -- the Chicken Place -- whose Chicken Place was it? Well, I can't remember all the names of them, you know. But these places were what you call famous, we called famous, because everybody in Harlem, and the people from downtown used to come uptown in those days and frequent these places, you know, because

in those days nobody was afraid to go anywhere. You'd see these people from downtown with high silk hats and the ladies in diamonds and furs and things, and just strolling down the street, you know, 3:00 or 4:00 o'clock in the morning, you know.
